newsitem.title: USA: US West Coast light crudes track higher WTI prices.
newsitem.headline: US West Coast light crudes track higher WTI prices.

text.p: Prices for U.S. West Coast light crudes tracked a 20-cent rise in bellwether West Texas Intermediate, with buyers pessimistic about deals getting done amid poor margins.
"The mood is pretty dismal considering where margins are," a trader said, adding that demand would stay weak for ANS next month.
November cash WTI rose 20 cents from late Thursday to $22.25/22.65 a barrel, up on higher futures and last-minute demand for Friday's pipeline scheduling.

Outright prices for Alaska North Slope (ANS) crude tracked WTI and rose 20 cents, leaving the grade $22.25/22.65 a barrel. Official discounts for ANS remained unchanged at $2.30 a barrel under November WTI.
Ultramar Corp said it would bring down several hydroprocessing units late this week for an unspecified period of maintenance.
Wilmingtoncrude held at $18.90/19 a barrel today.
Kern River heavy crude also held, ranging $17.40.17.60 a barrel, with a major and large independent refiner rumored to offer cargoes. --David Brinkerhoff, Los Angeles energy +1 213 380 2014
